To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present a novel algorithm for learning purposeful behaviour, which is capable of learning goal directed behaviour in the absence and presence of rewards, and that it is especially suited for domains with sparse rewards.
the agent learns to explore the state space by constructing temporally-extended options, and these options help to learn a reward function that is very sparse.
we introduce a new algorithm that learns purposeful behaviour in environments where rewards are absent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1. How can an agent learn purposeful behaviour in a world with no explicit reward signal? 2. How can we learn behaviours that are useful when rewards are sparse?
the following question: how can we build agents capable of exhibiting purposeful behaviour in environments with no explicit reward signal?
how to learn purposeful behaviour in an environment where there are no rewards, or where rewards are so sparse as to be effectively absent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents a novel approach to learning behaviour in the absence rewards.
the proposed algorithm learns a suite of behaviours which can be used to explore the state space of the environment.
the proposed approach can learn purposeful behaviour in environments where reward is absent or very sparse, and is capable of exploring environments to discover reward.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated how to learn a purposeful policy for an agent that is not rewarded for its behaviour.
the agent learns to behave in a purposeful manner in the absence of reward.
we have demonstrated that it is possible for an agent to learn to behave intelligently in the absence of a reward signal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absence of reward does not imply the absence of purposeful behaviour.
purposeful behaviour can be learnt in the absence of reward signals, and that such purposeful behaviour can help in the learning of reward-based behaviour.
, even without rewards, it is possible for an agent to exhibit purposeful behaviour, and to learn behaviours that are useful for exploration. 01/01/2018 ∙ by Pedro A. Morales
